correctness.rationale: For each integer \(m\ge2\) and either field, the one-step convolution map \(L_\theta\) has Gram eigenvalues \(1+2|ab|\cos(k\pi/(m+1))\), uniformly separated from zero over unit projective coefficients. Spherical Beta projection gives a fixed-direction small-ball bound of order \(t^{\beta m}\); the projective net costs order \(t^{-\beta}\), so the upper least-singular-value exponent is \(\beta(m-1)\). The negative Gaussian-radius moment is finite. A bounded Gaussian chart with two free first samples and \(m-1\) complex or real recursion residuals has triangular Jacobian one and matching positive-density lower bound of order \(t^{\beta(m-1)}\). Homogeneity and a bounded-chart lower bound establish the same condition-number exponent. Layer-cake proves the exact inverse-moment cutoff, including divergence at equality. A standalone checker replayed 1305 finite exact arithmetic identities; the continuum conclusions follow from the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Quantitative persistency and robust data-driven inversion depend on small singular values, but ordinary rank-a.s. excitation provides no integrability guarantee. The sharp two-row finite-sample threshold identifies the exact additional Gaussian samples needed for finite mean and variance of worst-case linear noise amplification. The real/complex distinction makes a nontrivial geometric codimension split, and the proof handles the dependence due to overlapping observations instead of applying iid matrix results. A natural standalone stability diagnostic is determined exactly for all finite column counts, with no downstream controller theorem claimed.
